summary: This mishnah lists the people in charge of different jobs in the Beis HaMikdash, like the seals, the wine offerings, the lotteries, the gates, the music, the lechem hapanim and the ketores.

chunks.en: These are the people in charge in the Beis HaMikdash:
chunks.st: These are the officials who served in specific positions in the Temple:

chunks.en: Yochanan ben Pinchas was in charge of the seals,
chunks.st: Yoḥanan ben Pineḥas was responsible for the seals.
chunks.stMore: One who paid for a specific type of sacrificial item received a seal, which he presented to the Temple official in exchange for that item.

words.note: Tickets people bought to get the wine offerings for their korban.

chunks.en: Achiyah was in charge of the wine offerings,
chunks.st: Aḥiyya was responsible for the libations,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the wine, oil, and flour prepared with the level of ritual purity necessary for the libation offerings and the meal-offerings, which accompanied many animal offerings. Aḥiyya supplied the libations to those who presented the appropriate seal.

chunks.en: Matisyah ben Shmuel was in charge of the lotteries,
chunks.st: Matya ben Shmuel was responsible for the lotteries,
chunks.stMore: which were used to select priests for the various Temple services each day.

words.note: Choosing which Kohen does each job.

chunks.en: Pesachyah was in charge of the bird pairs.
chunks.st: Petaḥya was responsible for the pairs of birds,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the turtledoves or pigeons, brought by a zav, a zava, a woman after childbirth, and a leper. They placed the appropriate sum of money into the horn designated for this purpose, and each day Petaḥya oversaw the purchase of birds from that money and their sacrifice in the proper manner.

chunks.en: Pesachyah is Mordechai.
chunks.st: Incidentally, the Gemara mentions: Petaḥya is Mordecai from the book of Esther.

chunks.en: Why was he called Pesachyah?
chunks.st: And why was he called Petaḥya, which resembles the word for opening [petaḥ]?

chunks.en: Because he would open up hard topics and explain them,
chunks.st: The reason is that he would open, i.e., elucidate, difficult topics and interpret them to the people,

chunks.en: and he knew seventy languages.
chunks.st: and because he knew all seventy languages known at the time.

chunks.en: Ben Achiyah was in charge of Kohanim with stomach sickness,
chunks.st: The mishna resumes the list of officials. Ben Aḥiyya was responsible for the care of the priests who suffered from intestinal disease.

chunks.en: Nechunya dug wells,
chunks.st: Neḥunya was the well digger for pilgrims on their way to Jerusalem for the Festivals.

words.note: Wells for people coming to Yerushalayim for Yom Tov.

chunks.en: Gevini was the caller,
chunks.st: Gevini was the Temple crier
chunks.stMore: who would awaken the priests and the Levites for their Temple duties.

words.note: He called out to wake the Kohanim and Levi'im for their work.

chunks.en: Ben Gever was in charge of locking the gates,
chunks.st: Ben Gever was responsible for locking the Temple gates in the evening and for unlocking them in the morning.

chunks.en: Ben Bevai was in charge of the wicks,
chunks.st: Ben Bevai was appointed over the shreds of garments,
chunks.stMore: which were formed into wicks for the Temple candelabra. He also supervised the twisting of those wicks into the appropriate thickness for the various nights during the different seasons of the year.

words.note: Made from old clothes of the Kohanim, for the Menorah.

chunks.en: Ben Arza was in charge of the cymbal,
chunks.st: Ben Arza was responsible for the cymbal,
chunks.stMore: which was rung as a signal that the Levites should commence their song.

words.note: A metal musical instrument, rung so the Levi'im would start to sing.

chunks.en: Hugras ben Levi was in charge of the singing,
chunks.st: Hugras ben Levi was responsible for the song. He taught and conducted the singers in the Temple.

chunks.he: בֵּית גַּרְמוּ עַל מַעֲשֵׂה לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים,
chunks.en: the family of Garmu was in charge of making the lechem hapanim,
chunks.st: The house of Garmu was responsible for the preparation of the shewbread;

chunks.en: the family of Avtinas was in charge of making the ketores,
chunks.st: the house of Avtinas was responsible for the preparation of the incense;

chunks.en: Elazar was in charge of the curtains,
chunks.st: and Elazar was responsible for weaving the Temple curtains;

chunks.en: and Pinchas was in charge of the clothing.
chunks.explain: He helped the Kohanim get dressed in their special clothes.
chunks.st: and Pineḥas was the valet,
chunks.stMore: who assisted the priests in fitting their clothes and dressing themselves for their Temple service.

summary: There must be at least three treasurers and seven trustees for the money of the Beis HaMikdash. People in charge of public money must be at least two, except for two special people everyone trusted.

chunks.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשְּׁלֹשָה גִּזְבָּרִין וּמִשִּׁבְעָה אֲמַרְכָּלִין,
chunks.en: There may not be fewer than three treasurers and seven trustees.
chunks.st: There must be no fewer than seven trustees [amarkolin] and three treasurers appointed over the Temple administration.

chunks.he: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין שְׂרָרָה עַל הַצִּבּוּר בְּמָמוֹן
chunks.en: And we do not make someone in charge of public money
chunks.st: And we do not appoint an authority over the public comprised

chunks.en: with less than two people,
chunks.st: of fewer than two people,

chunks.he: חוּץ מִבֶּן אֲחִיָּה שֶׁעַל חוֹלֵי מֵעַיִם
chunks.en: except for Ben Achiyah, who was in charge of stomach sickness,
chunks.st: except for ben Aḥiyya, who was responsible for healing priests who suffered from intestinal disease,

chunks.en: and Elazar, who was in charge of the curtains,
chunks.st: and Elazar, who was responsible for the weaving of the Temple curtains.

chunks.en: because most of the people accepted them.
chunks.st: The reason for these exceptions is that the majority of the public accepted these men upon themselves
chunks.stMore: as officials who served without the assistance of even a single partner.

summary: There were seals with words written on them, each for a different kind of wine offering. This mishnah tells what was written on them and which korbanos each one was for.
stIntro: This mishna provides details of the functions performed by Yoḥanan ben Pineḥas and Aḥiyya, the officials mentioned in the first mishna of this chapter, which concerns the seals and libations.

chunks.en: There were four seals in the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: There were four seals in the Temple
chunks.stMore: that confirmed that the bearer had paid for the libations that accompanied his offering.

chunks.en: and on them was written,
chunks.st: And one of the following inscriptions was written on them:

chunks.en: "Calf," "Male,"
chunks.st: Calf; male, i.e., a ram;

chunks.en: "Kid," "Sinner."
chunks.st: kid; and sinner,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a leper, as leprosy is a punishment for one of seven sins (see Arakhin 16a). Conversely,

words.note: Here it means a metzora, a person with tzaraas.

chunks.en: Ben Azzai says,
chunks.st: ben Azzai says:

chunks.en: There were five,
chunks.st: There were five seals,

chunks.en: and written on them in Aramaic was:
chunks.st: and the following was written upon them in Aramaic, not Hebrew:

chunks.he: עֵגֶל, זָכָר, גְּדִי, חוֹטֵא דַּל, וְחוֹטֵא עָשִׁיר.
chunks.en: "Calf," "Male," "Kid," "Poor sinner," and "Rich sinner."
chunks.st: Calf, male, kid, poor sinner, and rich sinner.

chunks.en: The "Calf" seal is used for the wine offerings of cattle,
chunks.st: The mishna explains the significance of each of the four aforementioned seals. The calf seal serves as a payment receipt for libations of cattle offerings,

chunks.en: big or small, male or female.
chunks.st: whether they are large or small, male or female,
chunks.stMore: as all offerings from the cow family are accompanied by the same libation.

chunks.en: The "Kid" seal is used for the wine offerings of sheep and goats,
chunks.st: The kid seal serves for libations of sheep or goat offerings,

chunks.en: big or small, male or female,
chunks.st: whether large or small, male or female,

chunks.en: except for rams.
chunks.st: except for those of rams aged thirteen months and older.

chunks.he: זָכָר מְשַׁמֵּשׁ עִם נִסְכֵּי אֵילִים בִּלְבָד.
chunks.en: The "Male" seal is used only for the wine offerings of rams.
chunks.st: The ram seal, which was earlier called the male seal, serves exclusively for ram libations.

chunks.en: The "Sinner" seal is used for the wine offerings
chunks.st: The sinner seal serves for libations of the

chunks.en: of the three animals of a metzora.
chunks.explain: A metzora brings three animals when he becomes tahor.
chunks.st: three animal offerings of a leper, for the completion of his purification.

summary: To get wine offerings, a person paid Yochanan for a seal and gave the seal to Achiyah. In the evening they checked the money against the seals, and hekdesh always came out ahead.

chunks.en: Someone who wants wine offerings
chunks.st: One who seeks libations for his offering

chunks.en: goes to Yochanan,
chunks.st: goes to Yoḥanan,

chunks.en: who is in charge of the seals,
chunks.st: the official who was responsible for the seals,

chunks.he: נוֹתֵן לוֹ מָעוֹת וּמְקַבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ חוֹתָם.
chunks.en: gives him money, and gets a seal from him.
chunks.st: and gives him the appropriate sum of money and receives a seal from him.

chunks.en: Then he comes to Achiyah,
chunks.st: With that seal he subsequently comes to Aḥiyya,

chunks.en: who is in charge of the wine offerings,
chunks.st: who was responsible for the libations,

chunks.he: וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ חוֹתָם וּמְקַבֵּל מִמֶּנּוּ נְסָכִים.
chunks.en: and gives him the seal and gets the wine offerings from him.
chunks.st: and gives him Yoḥanan’s seal and receives his libations from him.

chunks.en: In the evening they meet each other,
chunks.st: In the evening, Yoḥanan and Aḥiyya would get together to reconcile their accounts,

chunks.en: and Achiyah takes out the seals
chunks.st: and Aḥiyya would take out the seals he had received

chunks.en: and gets money in their place.
chunks.st: and accept the money Yoḥanan had received in exchange for them.

chunks.he: וְאִם הוֹתִירוּ הוֹתִירוּ לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ. וְאִם פָּחָתוּ,
chunks.en: If there was extra, the extra goes to hekdesh. But if there was too little,
chunks.st: If the money was less than the value of the seals, they were less to him, i.e., Yoḥanan would bear the loss,

chunks.en: Yochanan would pay from his own house,
chunks.st: and Yoḥanan would have to pay the difference to the Temple treasury from his own property. And if there was some money left over, i.e., the total money was greater than the value of the seals, they were left over to the benefit of the Temple treasury of consecrated property,

chunks.en: because hekdesh always has the upper hand.
chunks.st: as the Temple treasury always has the upper hand.

summary: If someone lost his seal, they waited until evening to see if there was extra money for it. The day was written on the seals so cheaters could not use old ones.

chunks.en: Someone who lost his seal
chunks.st: With regard to one who lost his seal that he purchased from Yoḥanan,

chunks.en: they wait for him until evening.
chunks.st: Yoḥanan and Aḥiyya would wait to resolve his problem until the evening.

chunks.en: If they find extra money worth his seal,
chunks.st: And when they added their accounts in the evening, if they found for him a surplus of money equivalent to the value of his seal,

chunks.en: they give him the wine offerings.
chunks.st: they would give him the corresponding libations.

chunks.en: And if not, he gets nothing.
chunks.st: And if not, they would not give him libations.

chunks.he: וְשֵׁם הַיּוֹם כָּתוּב עֲלֵיהֶן מִפְּנֵי הָרַמָּאִין:
chunks.en: The name of the day was written on them because of cheaters.
chunks.explain: So no one could use an old seal from another day.
chunks.st: And the name of the day of the week was written upon the seals because of the cheats.
chunks.stMore: They might try to use old seals that had been lost by the Temple officials or by someone who had brought an offering at an earlier date, so as to receive libations in a deceitful manner.

summary: There were two special rooms in the Beis HaMikdash. In one, people secretly gave tzedakah for poor people from good families, and in the other, people gave vessels to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: There were two rooms in the Beis HaMikdash:
chunks.st: There were two special chambers in the Temple,

chunks.en: one was the secret room,
chunks.st: one called the chamber of secret gifts

chunks.en: and one was the room of vessels.
chunks.st: and the other one called the chamber of vessels.

chunks.en: In the secret room, people who fear sin
chunks.st: The mishna explains the purpose of these chambers. In the chamber of secret gifts, sin-fearing people

chunks.en: put money in it secretly,
chunks.st: put money secretly

chunks.he: וַעֲנִיִּים בְּנֵי טוֹבִים מִתְפַּרְנְסִים מִתוֹכָהּ בַּחֲשַׁאי.
chunks.en: and poor people from good families get their support from it secretly.
chunks.explain: So no one would be embarrassed.
chunks.st: and poor people of noble descent support themselves from it secretly.

chunks.en: The room of vessels:
chunks.st: With regard to the chamber of vessels,

chunks.he: כָּל מִי שֶׁהוּא מִתְנַדֵּב כֶּלִי, זוֹרְקוֹ לְתוֹכָהּ.
chunks.en: whoever gives a vessel as a gift throws it inside.
chunks.st: anyone who donates a vessel to the Temple drops it inside that chamber,

chunks.he: וְאַחַת לִשְׁלשִׁים יוֹם, גִּזְבָּרִין פּוֹתְחִין אוֹתָהּ.
chunks.en: Once every thirty days the treasurers open it.
chunks.st: and once every thirty days the treasurers open it.

chunks.he: וְכָל כְּלִי שֶׁמּוֹצְאִין בּוֹ צֹרֶךְ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת,
chunks.en: Any vessel they find useful for fixing the Beis HaMikdash
chunks.st: And any vessel that they found for it a use for Temple maintenance,

chunks.en: they keep it.
chunks.st: they leave it for that purpose,

chunks.he: וְהַשְּׁאָר נִמְכָּרִין בִּדְמֵיהֶן וְנוֹפְלִין לְלִשְׁכַּת בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת:
chunks.en: The rest are sold, and their money goes to the room for fixing the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: and the rest are sold, and their monetary value is allocated to Temple maintenance.
